intro: The press, radio and television in more detail, and giving your opinion of what you see.
p.el locutor.nota: The feminine form is la locutora.
p.el culebrón.nota: Colloquial in Spain; telenovela is also widely used.
p.estar informado.nota: Informado/a agrees in gender and number with the person.
p.el telediario.nota: Common in Spain; el informativo or el noticiero are also used.
p.internet.nota: Internet is used with either masculine or feminine article depending on region and style; this course normally omits the article.
p.la noticia: the news item; the piece of news
p.enterarse.nota: Enterarse de algo means to find out about something; the dialogue uses me he enterado por la prensa.
b1.texto:
**Los medios de comunicación** are **la prensa**, **la radio**, **la televisión** and **internet**.

In a newspaper there are **titulares**, **noticias**, **artículos** de opinión, **reportajes** and **entrevistas**. A paper **publica** una noticia.

On television, **las cadenas** show **el telediario**, **documentales**, **concursos**, **debates**, **series** and **culebrones**. A radio station is **una emisora**, and the voice is **el locutor**.

To judge: es **fiable** / **poco fiable**; es **objetivo**; es **telebasura**; **me informo por** la radio.

To say how you know: **me he enterado por** la prensa; **según** el periódico; **lo han dicho en** la radio.

Opinions with the mood you know: **creo que** hay demasiada publicidad; **no creo que** esa noticia **sea** verdad; **me parece mal que** no **citen** la fuente.
b2.titulo: Where do you get your news?
b2.f0: How do you keep informed? I don't watch the TV news any more.
b2.f1: I read the press on my phone and listen to a news station.
b2.f2: And do you think everything they publish is reliable?
b2.f3: No. I don't think all the headlines are true. I always check the source.
b2.f4: It bothers me that there's so much trash TV.
b2.f5: Well, last night they showed a very good documentary on the public channel.
b4.pregunta: Complete: I don't think that news is true.
b4.o0.refuerzo: A negative opinion takes the subjunctive.
b4.o1.refuerzo: No creo que takes the subjunctive, so sea; the indicative es does not fit.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Será is future; after no creo que the subjunctive sea is needed.
b5.o1.refuerzo: That is usually a TV channel.
b6.o0: I found out from the press.
b6.o2: I am interested in the press.
b7.pregunta: Which word describes a source you can trust?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Fiable means reliable, a source you can trust.
b8.pregunta: Complete: it bothers me that there is so much advertising.
b8.o0.refuerzo: A feeling takes the subjunctive: hay becomes haya.
b8.o1.refuerzo: After me molesta que, the subjunctive.
b8.o2.refuerzo: After me molesta que, the present subjunctive.
b9.traduccion: I always check the source of the news.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write your opinion on the news media in your country: which you trust and which you do not.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Summarise aloud a news story you have read or heard this week, and say what you think of it.
b6.o0.explicacion: Me he enterado por la prensa means I learnt about it from the newspapers.
